question: Should OpenClaw adopt local, container, reverse-proxy, and node-mode as the initial named, release-tested hosting support catalog above the separate readiness contract?
rationale: This is a new cross-cutting deployment and support promise with configuration, upgrade, and proxy-trust consequences; source review cannot determine whether these four postures are the intended permanent product boundary.

options.title: Sponsor the four-profile catalog
options.body: Accept the RFC direction, contingent on the linked core stack preserving unprofiled behavior and completing exact packaged conformance proof.

options.title: Keep readiness generic
options.body: Accept or continue RFC 0018 without built-in hosting profiles, leaving deployments to direct readiness-criterion selection.

options.title: Narrow the initial catalog
options.body: Approve only the postures maintainers are prepared to support and require a revised RFC for deferred profiles.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the four-profile catalog
recommendation.body: Accept the RFC direction, contingent on the linked core stack preserving unprofiled behavior and completing exact packaged conformance proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The author has carried the RFC and linked implementation-stack updates and is the clearest available routing contact for the decision packet.
